title: Landlord texted: 12 minutes or collapse

parts:
[[12 MINUTES LEFT]] My landlord just texted: “Leave the house in twelve minutes or the walls will collapse.” I stare at the screen, pulse thudding. The kitchen clock reads 3:14 PM. I slam my thumb on the call button—one ring, then silence. Outside, the wind screams, rattling the cracked panes.

[[DAY 1 · 3:15 PM]] I bolt down the hallway, phone clenched, a low creak echoing behind the drywall. My shoe catches the ragged rug; fibers rip, teeth of the carpet scrape the floor. The ceiling flickers, a soft hum swelling into a whine that vibrates through the plaster. 

[[RULE 1 · NO PANIC]] My brain flashes the lease: “No early termination without notice.” The fine print glints like a trap. At the end of the corridor the hallway door hangs ajar, a black slit swallowing the light. I shove it open; a cold draft slaps my cheek.

[[3 MINUTES LEFT]] Shadows crawl along the walls. A muffled thud drums from the living room—something massive slamming onto the floor. My phone buzzes: “Don’t look up.” I stare upward. The ceiling groans, deeper, as if bones are cracking.

A cracked tile falls from above, landing with a metallic clatter just inches from my head. I gasp, heart snapping. The hallway lights flicker out, plunging me into darkness—

[[STAKES ESCALATE]] I’m still in the hallway, the ticking clock now at eight minutes. The text on my phone reads “Don’t look up.” I swallow, feeling bile rise. I swing the hallway door wide, peeking into the living room. The couch is overturned, a lamp shattered, glass glittering like ice. A faint smell of stale coffee mixes with dust. [[RULE 2 · INVESTIGATE]] I spot a thin line of light seeping from under the bedroom door. My pulse spikes. I inch toward the vent cover on the wall, fingers trembling as I pry it loose. A narrow duct yawns, dark and cold. I slip my hand inside, feeling a rough rope tangled with something metallic. [[5 MINUTES LEFT]] A low chuckle echoes from the vent, distant but unmistakable. I pull the cover back, and a scrap of paper slides out, stamped with a strange symbol – a circle with a slash. My mind races: Is this a warning or a clue? The front door bursts open, the landlord’s silhouette framed by bright sunlight. He shouts, “What are you doing? Get out now!” I stare at him, then at the vent, the clock now at three minutes. I realize the vent leads to a hidden room I’ve never seen. [[CLUE DISCOVERED]] I have to decide: run with the landlord or crawl into the unknown.

[[FINAL SHOWDOWN]] The clock is counting down, and if I don’t stop them now, the whole building collapses.
I’m crouched in the vent, the metal humming under my breath. The landlord’s voice booms behind me, "Twelve minutes or it all comes down!"
I yank the rope. A hidden panel slides open, revealing a cramped attic.
A lone figure hunches over a laptop, eyes glued to a live feed of my apartment. He whispers, "Almost there."
He turns – gaunt, scar slicing his cheek, hoodie pulled low. He lifts a small remote. The walls shudder louder.
A crack erupts in the ceiling above my head. I gasp. He smirks, "The lease is mine now. You’re just a pawn."
I scramble backward, the vent trembling, a slab of plaster falling inches from my forehead.
Suddenly the landlord bursts in, swinging a fire extinguisher. "Enough!" he roars.
Foam sprays into the vent, drenching the hidden tenant’s gear. The remote fizzles, the tremor stops.
The scarred man curses, "You won’t get away with this," and darts toward a concealed door, disappearing into the walls.
I stare at the landlord, panting, eyes wild. "I… I didn’t know," he stammers, "they forced me."
Water drips from the cracked ceiling. My phone buzzes—last text still glowing: "Don’t look up."
I look up. The ceiling hangs precariously, every beam groaning.
I turn to the camera, heart pounding, and ask: Did I do the right thing, or should I have run? What’s your verdict?

premise.hook: My landlord just texted: "Leave the house in 12 minutes or the walls will collapse."
premise.twist: The structural failure is a staged test by a hidden tenant watching through the vents, trying to force me out so they can claim the lease.
premise.debate: Viewers will argue whether the narrator should flee immediately or try to expose the scam, and whether the landlord is complicit or a victim too.
